claim: The Perhentians are two car-free jungle islands off Terengganu — Kecil (livelier) and Besar (quieter) — reached only by boat; reefs have visibly declined and plastic pollution is a real problem.
quote: Pulau Perhentian Kecil... and Pulau Perhentian Besar... no cars or roads.

claim: Coral View Island Resort sits on Perhentian Besar's Teluk Pauh with turtle-snorkelling off the beach — a good comfortable-couple base.
quote: Coral View Island Resort, Perhentian Besar.

claim: Tuna Bay Island Resort on Perhentian Besar's Teluk Pauh offers half/full-board beachfront chalets on the quieter island.
quote: Tuna Bay Island Resort, Perhentian Besar.

claim: A full-day boat snorkel tour runs about RM150 (~€32) and hits Shark Point, Turtle Point, the coral garden, the lighthouse and the fishing village.
quote: Perhentian snorkeling day trip price 2026 RM150.

claim: Coral Bay on Perhentian Kecil's west side has the islands' best sunset.
quote: Coral Bay is the place to watch the sunset.

claim: Bioluminescent plankton night swims are possible off Long Beach on dark/new-moon nights.
quote: see glow-in-the-dark plankton in Malaysia.

claim: Kuala Terengganu's Crystal Mosque and Islamic Civilisation Park hold the region's real heritage, worth a day on the way in or out.
quote: Crystal Mosque, Taman Tamadun Islam, Kuala Terengganu.

claim: The NE monsoon shuts most resorts, dive shops and boats roughly Nov–Feb/Mar; April–June is the sweet spot (calm seas, fewer crowds), Jul–Sep is busiest.
quote: November should be avoided at all costs... the islands run March to October.

claim: There are no ATMs on either island and power is generator-run; bring all your cash from the mainland and confirm 24-hour electricity/aircon.
quote: There are no ATMs on the islands. Bring cash.

claim: The Perhentian season runs roughly March–October, with the best diving visibility in the drier months.
quote: best time to visit the Perhentian Islands.

claim: Hari Raya Aidilfitri 2026 falls ~20–23 March, a nationwide break landing just as the islands reopen — expect a domestic surge.
quote: Hari Raya Aidilfitri 2026 public holidays.

claim: Hari Raya Aidiladha 2026 (27–28 May) falls mid-season and brings a domestic-tourist bump; book ahead.
quote: Hari Raya Haji 2026 falls on 27 May.

claim: In mid-2026 €1 ≈ RM4.7 (verify on arrival).
quote: ECB euro reference exchange rate, Malaysian ringgit.

claim: A one-time marine park conservation fee of RM30 per foreign adult (RM15 child) is paid at the Kuala Besut jetty.
quote: Conservation charge: RM30 foreign adult.

claim: The speedboat from Kuala Besut jetty is ~RM40 one-way / ~RM70–80 return, ~30–40 min, with the last boat off the islands at 16:00.
quote: Fare RM40 one-way... last boat from the islands 16:00.

claim: From KL the practical route is a ~1h flight to Kota Bharu, then a taxi/transfer to Kuala Besut and the boat.
quote: fly Kuala Lumpur to Kota Bharu, then transfer to Kuala Besut.

claim: A direct daily bus links the Cameron Highlands (Tanah Rata) to Kuala Besut (~6h); from Langkawi there is no direct east-coast route.
quote: direct bus from the Cameron Highlands to Kuala Besut.

claim: Island eating is warung-and-BBQ, mostly resort-attached, with prices ~3× the mainland because nearly everything is brought in by boat.
quote: prices are around three times the mainland... stick to local food.

claim: The real Terengganu food prize is on the mainland — a breakfast crawl of nasi dagang, keropok lekor and satar around Kuala Besut / Kuala Terengganu.
quote: the Terengganu food crawl: nasi dagang, keropok lekor, satar.

claim: The Perhentian Marriott (opened ~2024, on Kecil) is the only international-standard resort with pools and full service; there are no true design hotels.
quote: Perhentian Marriott Resort & Spa.

claim: Alunan Resort (hillside, Kecil, all-inclusive) is one of the few genuinely characterful boutique stays.
quote: Alunan Resort, Perhentian Kecil.

claim: Crocodile Rock Villas (Kecil, near Coral Bay) is a jungle-glamping character stay whose bistro is the islands' best kitchen and strongest for vegetarians.
quote: Crocodile Rock Villas, Perhentian Kecil.

claim: Turtle Sanctuary Beach on Perhentian Besar is the highest-rated beach, with green turtles almost guaranteed in the late afternoon (after ~16:30).
quote: Turtle Sanctuary Beach... turtles almost guaranteed in the afternoon.

claim: Shark Point reliably shows blacktip reef sharks and is a headline snorkel site.
quote: Shark Point... blacktip reef sharks.

claim: The Windmill viewpoint hike (30–40 min from Long Beach) gives Kecil's only real panorama.
quote: jungle hike to the windmill viewpoint on Perhentian Kecil.

claim: Non-divers can do a Discover Scuba try-dive for about RM250 (~€54).
quote: Discover Scuba Diving RM250.

claim: There are no roads or cars on the islands — you walk short jungle paths or flag a water-taxi (~RM15–25 a hop).
quote: no public transport... water taxis and walking trails.

claim: Bungalow break-ins are reported and there is little police presence — split your cash across bags.
quote: petty theft... no real police presence.

claim: The Perhentian Turtle Project runs conservation work and visitor/volunteer engagement on the islands.
quote: Perhentian Turtle Project.

claim: Bidong Island, once a Vietnamese refugee camp described as among the most densely populated places on earth, is a sobering offbeat day-trip.
quote: Bidong Island... Vietnamese refugees.

claim: The Perhentians are one of Asia's cheapest places to learn to dive — a PADI Open Water course is about RM1,350 (~€293).
quote: PADI Open Water course RM1,350.
